To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the real exchange rates of the developing economies are determined by terms of trade, trade openness, capital inflows and productivity shocks.

(1) The real exchange rate of Bangladesh is not stationary, (2) There is a long run relationship among real exchange rate, trade openness, financial openness, government consumption, terms of trade and productivity, (3) Real exchange rate appreciates in response changes in terms of Trade and Productivity, (4) Real exchange rate depreciates in response changes in Trade Openness and Financial Openness, (5) Government Consumption has a negative but insignificant effect on Real Exchange rate.
the exchange rate of a country is determined by the changes in the terms of trade, the productivity shocks, government consumption spending, trade openness and financial openness.

the determinants of real exchange rate and their relative importance.
the determinants of the real exchange rate of developing countries.
the sources of movements of real effective exchange rates (REER) of developing countries.

the results obtained in this paper are consistent with the theoretical predictions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the REER appreciates with the increase in terms of trade and productivity and depreciates in response to changes of government spending, trade openness and financial openness.
we found a significant effect of terms of trade, trade openness, capital flows, government spending and productivity shocks on real exchange rate of five developing countries.

real exchange rates are not determined solely by the real fundamentals.
